name: Sheng Ji
description: Sheng Ji (Tractor / Level Up) is a Chinese point-trick game family with dynamic trump rank and suit each round. The standard form uses four players in fixed partnerships and two decks with jokers.
deck: Two 54-card decks (including jokers) in the common four-player form

overview.description: Sheng Ji (Tractor / Level Up) is a Chinese point-trick game family with dynamic trump rank and suit each round. The standard form uses four players in fixed partnerships and two decks with jokers.

history.origins: Sheng Ji developed as a Chinese point-trick game family and spread across regions with many house-rule systems.
timeline: 20th century: Regional variants of Sheng Ji become established in China.
Late 20th century: Tractor and related names become common in diaspora communities.
Present: Online platforms popularize multiple rule sets and team formats.
history.cultural: Sheng Ji is a major social partnership card game in Chinese communities, often played in long multi-round sessions.
history.evolution: Rules diverged by region on bidding strength, kitty size, no-trump handling, and score-to-rank advancement thresholds.

setup.players: Usually 4 players in fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite).
setup.deck: Commonly two full decks with jokers (108 cards total).
setup.dealing: Players draw one card at a time during deal; in two-deck four-player games, each player gets 25 cards and 8 cards remain as kitty/bottom.

rules.objective: Raise your partnership rank from 2 upward (often to Ace) by winning rounds while controlling opponents' trick points.
rules.gameplay: Each round establishes dominant rank and usually a dominant suit through bidding. Declarers take the kitty and discard back to kitty size. Trick play then proceeds with strict follow/combination constraints based on lead pattern and trump structure. Opponents' captured point cards (5s, 10s, Kings) determine whether declarers keep deal and advance or defenders seize momentum.
keyRules: Dynamic trump rank each round changes comparative card power.
Only 5s, 10s, and Kings score points in tricks.
Round control shifts based on opponents' point total thresholds.

strategy.basic: Track point cards and avoid giving away cheap 5/10/K captures in uncertain tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Use bidding pressure and trump timing to control lead and force weak combinations from defenders.
strategy.advanced: Plan long round tempo around rank advancement math, kitty information, and partnership signaling through legal pattern choices.
tips: Point counting (especially opponents' totals) is mandatory for strong play.
Trump exhaustion timing often determines whether late point tricks swing the round.

variations.name: Tractor (Double Deck)
variations.description: Most common partnership form with two decks, tractors/chains, and fixed partnerships.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses same engine as base; source does not specify numeric or config overrides.

variations.name: Zhao Pengyou (Finding Friends)
variations.description: Dealer calls partner cards in larger-player games with fluid partnerships.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant differs in partnership call; source does not document engine constant overrides.

scoring.description: Only point cards score in tricks: 5s, 10s, and Kings. Round outcomes and level advancement depend on opponents' total captured points and variant thresholds.
scoring.winCondition: Advance your partnership rank above the agreed target (commonly from 2 toward Ace) before opponents do.

synthesis.shortDescription: Sheng Ji is a Chinese dynamic-trump point-trick family where partnerships bid, play tractors and combinations, and advance rank by controlling opponents' point captures.
